Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on termination / data return exhibit

Ben / Aditya — thanks. Initial legal guidance below; I tracked comments in the attached draft. High-level answers: 1) Data return window: propose an export period of 30 days for customer-requested export of persistent data (models metadata, embeddings, customer objects), with certified deletion of customer-specific logs and KV cache within 90 days post-termination unless required for audit/retention by law. We should avoid a blanket immediate deletion clause; preserve a short retention period to support transition and audit requests. 2) Subprocessors: our standard is to provide a signed subprocessing exhibit that lists major subprocessors (cloud provider, backup storage, telemetry vendor) but we reserve the right to provide a redacted live list when there are frequent changes; we commit to notify customers 30 days before material changes.

I inserted a cross-reference to the liability cap section: recommend explicit statement that transition assistance obligations do not increase the liability cap beyond the amounts in the main agreement. Also added a clause about cost recovery: reasonable, documented transition fees beyond the 30-day assistance period.

Aditya — please see comments on the embedded/kv-cache handling (paragraph 4). If you can confirm practical timelines for producing a KV-prefix export and whether embeddings can be exported as a batch within the 30-day window, we can finalize.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_Termination_Exhibit_v2.docx (tracked changes)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on termination / data return exhibit

Laura / Ben — technical confirmation below. For typical deployments: 1) Persistent customer artifacts (indexes, embeddings stored in object storage, user metadata) can be exported in standard formats (S3 export .tar + manifest) within 7–14 business days by default if a data export request is initiated; 2) KV cache and transient inference caches are ephemeral — we can snapshot and export what is feasible but it requires coordination and may not be complete; we should be explicit that cache exports are best-effort and may exclude ephemeral entries. 3) Logs (request traces) are retained per retention policy; we can provide an export for a negotiated timeframe.

On subprocessors: we maintain a canonical subprocessor registry; for enterprise customers we can provide a signed exhibit enumerating major entities (cloud provider, telemetry) and a separate redacted live list for internal changes. Producing the signed exhibit is operationally fine but will require a one-week turnaround to pull contractual copies from vendor agreements.

I've attached a diagram showing where persistent data vs ephemeral cache lives in the stack. That should help negotiations.

Aditya Rao
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
attachments: Data_Subprocessing_Diagram.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarifications on termination / data return exhibit

Maya — thanks for patience. Please find attached our consolidated response and two exhibits: 1) Termination & Data-Return Exhibit (v2) — Laura added tracked redlines and language clarifying the 30-day export window plus certified deletion within 90 days for logs/cache except where retention is legally required; 2) Data Subprocessing Diagram — Aditya confirmed export timelines and the approach to signed vs redacted subprocessor lists.

High-level summary of positions we can commit to today: * Export: 30-day customer export for persistent artifacts; operational export completion typically 7–14 business days; * Cache: export best-effort, may be partial; explicit "best-effort" language added; * Subprocessors: we will provide a signed exhibit listing major subprocessors and a redacted live list for changes, with 30 days notice for material changes; * Transition assistance: 30 days included, reasonable fees thereafter; * Liability: transition obligations do not expand the liability cap in the main agreement.

Next steps: if the exhibit looks acceptable, we can issue a DocuSign package for the exhibit + order form. If you need a signed subprocessor exhibit, allow one week for us to assemble vendor copies.

Proposed timeline: Confirm by Jan 19 (one week) so procurement can process in time for the target Feb 1 start.

Best,
Ben
